import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm, t, skewnorm

strategies = [
    {
        'title': 'Aggressive 4th-Down Decisions',
        'family': 'normal',
        'params': {'mu': 0.5, 'sigma': 0.357},
        'most_plausible': 0.5
    },
    {
        'title': 'Early-Down Play-Action Passes',
        'family': 'normal',
        'params': {'mu': 0.7, 'sigma': 0.306},
        'most_plausible': 0.7
    },
    {
        'title': 'Two-High Safety Shells',
        'family': 'normal',
        'params': {'mu': 0.3, 'sigma': 0.306},
        'most_plausible': 0.3
    },
    {
        'title': 'Momentum-Stopping Timeouts',
        'family': 'skew_normal',
        'params': {'xi': -0.1, 'omega': 0.5, 'alpha': 2.0},
        'most_plausible': 0.2
    },
    {
        'title': 'Permanent No-Huddle Tempo',
        'family': 'skew_normal',
        'params': {'xi': 0.5, 'omega': 0.6, 'alpha': 2.0},
        'most_plausible': 0.8
    },
    {
        'title': 'Amoeba Pressure Defense',
        'family': 'student_t',
        'params': {'nu': 4.0, 'mu': 0.4, 'sigma': 0.5036},
        'most_plausible': 0.4
    }
]

x = np.linspace(-3, 4, 1000)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 8))
axes = axes.flatten()

for ax, strat in zip(axes, strategies):
    if strat['family'] == 'normal':
        mu = strat['params']['mu']
        sigma = strat['params']['sigma']
        dist = norm(mu, sigma)
        pdf = dist.pdf(x)
        low = dist.ppf(0.025)
        high = dist.ppf(0.975)
        label = f'Normal(μ={mu:.3f}, σ={sigma:.3f})'
    elif strat['family'] == 'student_t':
        nu = strat['params']['nu']
        mu = strat['params']['mu']
        sigma = strat['params']['sigma']
        dist = t(df=nu, loc=mu, scale=sigma)
        pdf = dist.pdf(x)
        low = dist.ppf(0.025)
        high = dist.ppf(0.975)
        label = f't(ν={nu}, μ={mu:.3f}, σ={sigma:.3f})'
    elif strat['family'] == 'skew_normal':
        xi = strat['params']['xi']
        omega = strat['params']['omega']
        alpha = strat['params']['alpha']
        dist = skewnorm(loc=xi, scale=omega, a=alpha)
        pdf = dist.pdf(x)
        low = dist.ppf(0.025)
        high = dist.ppf(0.975)
        label = f'SkewNormal(ξ={xi:.3f}, ω={omega:.3f}, α={alpha:.1f})'
    
    ax.plot(x, pdf, 'k-', linewidth=2)
    ax.fill_between(x, pdf, where=(x >= low) & (x <= high), color='skyblue', alpha=0.4, label='95% interval')
    ax.axvline(strat['most_plausible'], color='red', linestyle='--', label=f'Most plausible = {strat["most_plausible"]}')
    ax.set_title(strat['title'], fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xlabel('Change in own scoring margin (points)')
    ax.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=8)
    print(f'{strat["title"]}: {label}')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

quantity.description: Change in own-team expected single-game scoring margin from adopting the strategy
quantity.support: unbounded real; positive favors own team

prior.consistency_check: Most plausible 0.5 lies inside [-0.2, 1.2]; normal support is all reals, covering signed values.

distribution_family.justification: Effect should be roughly symmetric around a small positive mode, with thin tails because the upside is capped by extra possessions and downside limited by field-position value.
distribution_family.name: normal

strategies.rationale: Models show punting yields similar expected points as surrendering possession, while converting retains scoring opportunities and substantially raises win probability.
strategies.recommendation: Go for it on 4th-and-1 to 3 yards whenever past the opponent's 45-yard line, and occasionally from own territory in plus situations, following win-probability model recommendations.
strategies.title: Aggressive 4th-Down Decisions

prior.consistency_check: Most plausible 0.7 is inside [0.1, 1.3]; normal covers signed values.

distribution_family.justification: The effect is likely symmetric with little chance of extreme values; large upside would require defensive meltdowns, large downside would mean extreme interception luck, both improbable.
distribution_family.name: normal

strategies.rationale: Play-action consistently yields higher yards per attempt and lower interception rate than straight dropbacks, even when the run game is ineffective; it directly increases scoring.
strategies.recommendation: Use play-action passing on 1st and 2nd down regardless of run-game success, exploiting linebackers' run-fits to open intermediate routes.
strategies.title: Early-Down Play-Action Passes

prior.consistency_check: Most plausible 0.3 inside [-0.3, 0.9]; normal support covers signed values.

distribution_family.justification: The net benefit is likely small and symmetric; large deviations would require a league-wide shift in offensive scheme, which is unlikely in the short term.
distribution_family.name: normal

strategies.rationale: Data shows explosive plays are highly correlated with opponent scoring; two-high looks reduce deep completions without significantly increasing underneath efficiency, lowering opponent points per drive.
strategies.recommendation: Base out of two-high safety coverage (Cover 2, Quarters) to limit explosive passes and force offenses into long, methodical drives.
strategies.title: Two-High Safety Shells

prior.consistency_check: Mode ~0.2 inside interval; skew_normal has unbounded real support, covering signed values.

distribution_family.justification: Right skew captures a small chance of a large positive payoff if timeouts repeatedly cause failed conversions, while downside is bounded by lost clock value but can be significant.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: α=2.0 gives right skew; ξ and ω fitted numerically so mode ≈0.2 and central 95% mass ≈[-0.5, 0.9] (approximate).

strategies.rationale: Psychological disruption can lower conversion rates on key downs, leading to additional stops and a possession edge; this relies on coaching intuition about player psychology because public analytics on icing/timeout effect is sparse and mixed.
strategies.recommendation: Use timeouts on defense during opponent's critical 3rd-down plays to disrupt rhythm and force a mental reset, even at the expense of end-of-half clock management.
strategies.title: Momentum-Stopping Timeouts

prior.consistency_check: Mode ~0.8 inside interval; skew_normal support covers signed values.

distribution_family.justification: If the strategy works, the upside could be large as defenses tire and break down; downside is limited but non-trivial if it leads to quick three-and-outs and exposes own defense.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: α=2.0; ξ and ω fitted numerically to give mode ≈0.8 and 95% interval ≈[-0.3, 1.9].

strategies.rationale: Wearing down opponents leads to more explosive plays later in halves and can induce defensive penalties; public analytics is mixed on the net effect because faster drives also give the opponent more possessions, so this relies on a belief in fatigue and psychological pressure.
strategies.recommendation: Run the offense at a consistently fast pace (no-huddle, quick snaps) throughout the game, not just in two-minute drills, to wear down defenses and prevent substitutions.
strategies.title: Permanent No-Huddle Tempo

prior.consistency_check: μ=0.4 is inside [-1.0, 1.8]; student_t support covers all reals, signed values included.

distribution_family.justification: High variance and heavy tails reflect the possibility of either a game-breaking turnover-fest or repeated coverage busts; symmetric around a small positive mode.
distribution_family.name: student_t

strategies.rationale: Chaotic pressure creates negative plays (sacks, interceptions) that strongly correlate with winning; public analytics is mixed because ultra-aggressive blitzing can also yield big gains, but this intuition accepts high variance as beneficial for a .500 team.
strategies.recommendation: Deploy a versatile 3-4 front with multiple stand-up defenders moving pre-snap and frequent overload blitzes, aiming to confuse the offensive line and force hurried decisions.
strategies.title: Amoeba Pressure Defense
